structure.subject: ROOT
structure.detail: The twelve bytes 'RIFF', a length, and 'AVI ' must open the file, in that order and at offset zero.
structure.description: An AVI file is a RIFF container whose form type is AVI.
structure.measured_gate: Measured: ffmpeg refuses any other signature or form type with 'Invalid data found'. The template stops at line 274 with a Warning and return -1 when the form is not 'AVI '.
structure.generation_note: Emit the twelve-byte header as a fixed head element, then fill ROOT.datalen last, once the whole file has been laid out.

structure.subject: LISTHEADER with type hdrl
structure.detail: A hdrl list must follow the RIFF header and must contain the avih chunk and one strl list per stream.
structure.description: The header list is where every stream is declared; without it there is nothing to decode.
structure.measured_gate: Measured: corrupting the avih chunk length by four bytes left the container parseable but produced ZERO streams, because the strl lists were then read from the wrong offset.
structure.generation_note: Emit it immediately after the RIFF header, before the movi list.

structure.subject: LISTHEADER with type strl
structure.detail: One strl list per stream, each containing strh, then strf, then strn, nested inside the hdrl list.
structure.description: Each stream is defined by its own list of header chunks.
structure.output_budget: Budget the whole hdrl list to about 64 KB, as a running total the generator increments by each strl list's full size - roughly 76 bytes of fixed chunks plus any codec extradata and palette. Stop adding streams when the budget is exhausted and set MainAVIHeader.dwStreams to the number actually emitted. No dimension, depth or codec field is capped to reach this figure.
structure.generation_note: Emit avih first, then one strl per stream. The template requires strn inside every strl (line 200) even though the format makes it optional.

structure.subject: strh before strf before strn
structure.detail: Within a strl list the chunks appear in exactly this order; the template reads them positionally.
structure.description: The stream header must precede the format chunk because its fccType decides how the format chunk is parsed.
structure.generation_note: Choose fccType first, then emit the matching strf variant, then strn.

structure.subject: LISTHEADER with type movi
structure.detail: A movi list must follow the header list and carries the media chunks.
structure.description: The movi list is where the actual video and audio data lives.
structure.generation_note: Emit it after hdrl and any JUNK padding, before idx1.

structure.subject: genericblock within the movi list
structure.detail: The movi list contains a run of media chunks, each an 8-byte header plus payload plus a pad byte when the payload length is odd.
structure.description: Media chunks are the inner repeating structure and the bulk of every AVI file.
structure.output_budget: Budget the movi list to about 4 MB, as a running total the generator computes BEFORE emitting anything: for uncompressed video one frame costs ((biWidth * biBitCount + 31) / 32) * 4 * abs(biHeight) + 8 bytes. When adding another frame would exceed the budget, stop adding frames. When even a single frame would exceed it, redraw the dimension and depth triple rather than clamping any of them - clamping is what turns a free dimension into a narrowed one. This is the only size-control mechanism for AVI.
structure.generation_note: Emit chunks while the budget allows, then set the movi LIST length so that the chunk sizes sum to exactly datalen - 4, which the template's exact-equality loop requires.

structure.subject: an empty movi list
structure.detail: The movi list must contain at least one media chunk.
structure.description: The template's movi loop is a do/while, so its body always executes once.
structure.measured_gate: ffmpeg itself accepts an empty movi list; the constraint is the template's alone.
structure.generation_note: Always emit at least one genericblock inside the movi list, or the template reads a chunk header from beyond the list.

structure.subject: genericblock chunks within the movi list
structure.detail: Media chunks run contiguously from the movi type field to the end of the list, separated only by RIFF pad bytes.
structure.description: RIFF has no inter-chunk framing beyond the 8-byte header and the even-alignment pad.
structure.generation_note: Nothing may be inserted between chunks except the pad byte that an odd payload length requires.

structure.subject: idx1HEADER
structure.detail: When present, the idx1 chunk comes after the movi list and is the last chunk in the file.
structure.description: The legacy AVI index is written after the media it indexes, because its offsets are only known then.
structure.measured_gate: Measured: files with and without idx1 decoded identically, and trailing bytes after it were ignored.
structure.generation_note: Emit it after the movi list, computing each entry's offset relative to the movi type field.

structure.subject: AVIINDEXENTRY within idx1HEADER
structure.detail: The index holds one 16-byte entry per media chunk, so its length is always a multiple of 16.
structure.description: The index is a flat array of fixed-size records.
structure.output_budget: Budget the index to 16 bytes times the number of media chunks actually emitted, which follows from the movi budget and needs no separate cap. A generator that stops adding frames stops adding entries at the same point.
structure.generation_note: Build the entries while emitting the movi chunks, recording each chunk's offset as it is written.

structure.subject: top-level chunk loop
structure.detail: After the RIFF header the file is a sequence of LIST, JUNK and idx1 chunks, walked until end of file.
structure.description: The template's main loop at lines 282-303 dispatches on the next four bytes and accepts only those three identifiers.
structure.output_budget: Covered by the movi and hdrl budgets, which together account for essentially the whole file. JUNK chunks are the one freely sized element here: budget all JUNK to about 64 KB, as a running total, since it is the format's designated filler and touches nothing a decoder validates.
structure.generation_note: Emit hdrl, then optional JUNK, then movi, then optional idx1. Any other FOURCC at this level makes the template print 'unknown chunk' and return -1 at line 302, so no other chunk type may appear.

structure.subject: any top-level chunk other than LIST, JUNK or idx1
structure.detail: The template's main loop accepts only these three identifiers and abandons the parse on anything else.
structure.description: Real AVI files also carry top-level chunks this template does not model.
structure.measured_gate: Measured: ffmpeg skips unknown top-level chunks by length without complaint, so this is a template restriction rather than a format rule.
structure.generation_note: Emit only LIST, JUNK and idx1 at the top level; the format would also permit others, but this template cannot parse them.

structure.subject: the three strf variants
structure.detail: Exactly one of strfHEADER_BIH, strfHEADER_WAVE and strfHEADER is emitted per stream, selected by AVIStreamHeader.fccType.
structure.description: The format chunk's interpretation is a three-way branch on the stream type.
structure.generation_note: Choose fccType, then emit the matching variant; the three are branches of the same if/else at lines 188-199.

structure.subject: ROOT.datalen and every chunk length
structure.detail: Every length field must be computed from the bytes actually emitted, innermost first.
structure.description: RIFF is a nested length-prefixed format with no resynchronisation markers.
structure.measured_gate: Measured: ffmpeg tolerated wrong lengths at the RIFF, LIST and strf levels but NOT at the avih level, where any deviation from 56 cost every stream in the file.
structure.generation_note: Emit payloads first, then lengths, working outwards: genericblock, then movi LIST, then RIFF. The template's movi loop additionally requires exactness where ffmpeg does not.

diversity_axes.why: The frame width, and the field ffmpeg actually uses. It multiplies into the row stride and so into the exact byte length every uncompressed frame must have, which makes it the direct counterpart of the GIF dimension that was narrowed and cost 1.7 points. The frame payload is computed from it; it is never shrunk to fit a frame.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Width sets the row stride ((W*bpp+31)/32)*4 and therefore how many padding bytes each row carries, which is a different branch of every raw-video row-copy loop. For the compressed codecs it sets the macroblock grid, so narrow and wide frames take different paths through the block loops.

diversity_axes.why: The frame height, and the only geometry field whose SIGN carries meaning: negative means top-down row order, which is a different row-indexing path. Measured, both signs decoded. It sizes the frame payload.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The magnitude sets the row count; the sign selects between bottom-up and top-down row ordering, which every raw-video decoder implements as two different loops.

diversity_axes.why: The pixel depth. It is the third factor in the frame-length product, and each value selects a different unpacking path: sub-byte masking at 1 and 4, palette lookup at 8, bitfield extraction at 16, and direct component reads at 24 and 32. Measured, all six decoded.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Selects the pixel unpacking routine and, below 8 bits, whether a palette is needed at all.
diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier B because the legal set is finite, but every member must be emitted - narrowing to 24 deletes the sub-byte and palettised paths entirely.

diversity_axes.why: The video codec, and by a wide margin the highest-leverage field in AVI. Measured, it selected eight different decoders in ffmpeg - rawvideo, msrle, mjpeg, msvideo1, cinepak, mpeg4, indeo3 - from a single DWORD. Pinning it to 0 would delete seven whole decoders from the reachable set.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: 0 drives the raw-video path, 1 and 2 the Microsoft RLE state machine, MJPG a complete JPEG decoder, MSVC and CRAM the Video 1 block decoder, cvid Cinepak, the MPEG-4 fourccs the full MPEG-4 Part 2 decoder, and an unregistered fourcc the no-decoder path.
diversity_axes.tier_note: Tier B with partial completeness, because the FOURCC space is open; an unlisted fourcc is still legal and reaches the unknown-codec path.

diversity_axes.why: The audio codec, and the audio-side counterpart of biCompression. Measured, it selected seven different decoders - pcm_u8, adpcm_ms, pcm_f32le, pcm_alaw, pcm_mulaw, adpcm_ima_wav, mp3, wmav2 - from one WORD.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Each tag instantiates a different audio decoder with different frame geometry and different block-alignment requirements.

diversity_axes.why: The channel count. Measured free at 1, 2 and 8, with 0 and 65535 reaching the decoder's own channel layout validation. Pinning it to 2 would delete mono and multichannel, which take different paths through every interleaving and downmix routine.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Sets the sample frame size and the channel layout; mono, stereo and multichannel are different interleaving loops.

diversity_axes.why: The sample rate - the archetypal Tier C field. Measured free from 1 to 192000, with 0 and 2^31 reaching the demuxer's sanity check. Narrowing it to 44100 and 48000 would fix the one field a resampler branches on.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Drives the resampler's rate-conversion path and the container's timestamp arithmetic.

diversity_axes.why: The audio sample depth. Together with nChannels it fixes the size of one PCM sample frame and therefore the byte length of every audio chunk, which makes it an audio-side counterpart of biBitCount. Measured, ffmpeg derives the real depth from the format tag rather than refusing any value here, so the whole span is free.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: 8 and 16 select different PCM sample readers, 32 the float reader, and 4 the ADPCM nibble unpacker; 0 tells a reader to take the depth from the codec instead, which is a different path again.

diversity_axes.why: The media chunk identifier. Measured completely free - even 'xxxx' decoded - but the convention it encodes is real: the two digits route the chunk to a stream and the suffix declares the data kind. Pinning it to '00dc' would delete multi-stream routing, the uncompressed-frame code 'db', the audio code 'wb' and the palette-change code 'pc' in one stroke.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: The digits select which stream a chunk belongs to, which in a multi-stream file decides which decoder receives it. The suffix distinguishes uncompressed from compressed video, audio, palette changes and subtitle text, each of which a strict reader dispatches differently.

diversity_axes.why: The declared stream count. Measured completely ignored by ffmpeg, which counts the strl lists it finds - so the number of streams a file actually carries is a free structural choice, and this field is just how the file describes it.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: A multi-stream file exercises the demuxer's stream routing, interleaving and per-stream timestamp machinery that a single-stream file never touches.

diversity_axes.why: The file-level flags. AVIF_MUSTUSEINDEX in particular changes a strict reader's entire strategy from walking the movi list to seeking via idx1, and AVIF_ISINTERLEAVED changes how it buffers. Measured never a gate, so the whole bit space is free.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: AVIF_HASINDEX and AVIF_MUSTUSEINDEX select between sequential and index-driven reading; AVIF_ISINTERLEAVED changes the buffering strategy; AVIF_TRUSTCKTYPE makes the chunk type codes authoritative.

diversity_axes.why: The time-base denominator. Together with dwRate it is the stream's frame rate, and measured every combination including the degenerate zeros decoded. Pinning it to 1 is the reflex that fixes the frame rate of every generated file.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Drives the container's timestamp arithmetic; non-integer rates such as 1001/30000 and the zero cases reach different branches of the duration and seek computation.

diversity_axes.why: The time-base numerator, with the same standing as dwScale; the pair must stay free to produce varied frame rates.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: As for dwScale: the ratio is the stream's samples per second.

diversity_axes.why: The declared frame count. Measured ignored - ffmpeg counts the chunks - so how many frames a file carries is a free choice that this field merely records. The count is what drives the movi budget.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: A reader that trusts it pre-allocates; one that does not counts chunks. Both paths exist and a disagreement between the two exercises the reconciliation code.

diversity_axes.why: The palette entry count for the indexed depths. It sizes the colour table that lives in exData, so it is a count feeding an allocation, and its only real restriction - not exceeding 2^biBitCount - comes from another field.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Drives the palette read loop and the colormap allocation; a short palette makes index validation meaningful.

diversity_axes.why: The format's designated filler. Measured skipped entirely, so it is the one place in an AVI file where arbitrary bytes of arbitrary length can vary without touching anything a decoder validates.
diversity_axes.decoder_paths: Skipped by length, so it contributes no branches of its own - but it lets a file's size and byte distribution vary freely, which is why the size budget lives here rather than on any geometry field.
